item.description:
Sidetone 1.1.3

The gap above the panel after moving between screens.

  • Going from the laptop screen to an external monitor could leave the panel with a band of empty space above it, until monitoring was switched off and on again. Opening the panel now sets it back to the right size.

Sidetone 1.1.2

Switching monitoring off closes the panel back up.

  • Turning monitoring off took the meters away and left a band of empty space above the panel, which made it look like it was floating below the menu bar. The panel now shrinks back to fit what is in it.

Sidetone 1.1.1

A fraction of the processor it used to take.

  • Monitoring with the panel closed took about fourteen per cent of a processor core. It now takes about one, which is battery back and a fan that stays quiet.
  • The panel costs less to keep open as well, and the meters move as smoothly as they did.
  • When a device you chose is unplugged, the panel names the device actually in use, rather than one that nothing is coming from.
